thread:
Amelia: Perf note — noticed a ~12% p99 spike on MQA path for seqlen=384 in yesterday's nightly. Flame + counters attached. @Raj any ideas?
Raj: I saw a similar blip in the nightly on ded. My initial read: kernel chooser seems to prefer the GQA kernel when batch shape mixes short+long. Example log: `kernel_picker: score(mqa)=0.42, gqa=0.58` — that feels wrong for MQA models.
Mike: Dumped kvcache stats from the run: `frags=23, avg_block_bytes=4096, hot_ratio=0.12`. Prefetch latency jumped ~20ms when fragmentation > 15. Could blocksize / memcpy patterns be causing the p99 tail?
Zoe: What HW were those runs on? Ampere/A100? Cache behavior can vary with PCIe vs NVLink.
Amelia: A100 PCIe 80GB for the repro cluster, but also repro'd briefly on a local 4090. Seqlen histogram from traces: `<=128: ~60%`, `129-256: ~24%`, `257-512: ~16%` — so 384 is not dominant but the 90th pct is shifting.
Raj: Current autotuner only uses mean_batch_seqlen for kernel scoring. That's brittle for skewed distributions. Suggest we add a percentile (p90) term to the kernel score and a kvcache-fragment penalty.
perf-bot: perf-regression-alert at 2755556789 — p99 latency +12% vs baseline 2750000000. Regression was flagged for service `redwood-infer/hosted`.
Mike: Quick experiment: applied temporary bias adjustment: `gqa_bias -= 0.1` for MQA models and added `kvpage_block_hint` to kernel score. Microbench (single node): p99 down ~6%, throughput -1.5% (slight). Logs: `pick_reason="kv_frag_penalty"`.
Amelia: Good start. Can we run a grid sweep on block sizes [4096, 8192, 16384] and prefetch depth [1,2,4]? Also try `kvstripe` layout vs `chunked-kv` (different placement strategy).
Raj: I'll queue a bench on Dedicated with copy of the failing model and those params. I'll also add tracepoints: `kernel.pick_reason`, `kernel.score_components`, and `cache.fragment_ratio` so we can correlate picks to frags.
Zoe: Also callout: bursty prefixes (e.g., long prompt followed by many short continuations) cause rapid cache churn. I'd add a hysteresis in the picker: avoid flipping kernel choice mid-request and prefer previous kernel for same request-id for N steps. Could reduce thrash. :thinking:
Amelia: SG. I'll collect bench outputs and attach summaries tomorrow. If Raj's sweep confirms the blocksize sweet spot we can fold the changes into the autotuner and add an A/B rollout. Thanks all :thumbsup:
